Extract, two paths: born-digital PDFs go text-layer-plus-LLM structured extraction against a per-type JSON schema; photos and scans go OCR first, with a vision-capable model for the worst 22% of PODs. Every field carries a confidence score.

Validate — deterministic rules, not model judgment, because rules are cheap, explainable to finance, and fail loudly: net + VAT must equal gross; supplier must exist in master data; shipment reference must match an open job; dates in plausible range; currency consistent with the lane. A model can be confidently wrong; an arithmetic check cannot.

Route: all fields green and confidence above the per-supplier threshold -> auto-post to the TMS through a rate-limit-aware poster (2 rps, idempotency keys, retry with backoff, never drop). Anything amber -> the exception UI: document image beside pre-filled fields, clerk corrects and posts in seconds — and every correction is captured as a labelled example, feeding evals and threshold tuning. The exception UI is a first-class product; it is where the last 25% of the value lives.

FastAPI fronts the exception UI and status endpoints; Postgres is the audit spine linking every TMS entry to its source image and approver. Eval gates in CI: the per-type field-level extraction suite must stay green for any prompt, model or parser change. Supplier folklore becomes routing rules — DHL rebills start human-only, because the clerks said so and they were right.

tasks.name: Risks
tasks.prompt: Produce a risk register with the top 8 risks. Each row: risk, likelihood (L/M/H), impact (L/M/H), mitigation, owner. The worst technical failure mode and the people risks must both appear.
tasks.expert:
- Confidently wrong amount auto-posted — M / H: the worst failure mode; a silent £12,000 error beats no automation for damage. Mitigation: arithmetic validation, 4-eyes review above £5k gross, per-supplier thresholds, daily reconciliation report to finance. Owner: engineering + finance.
- POD quality floor — H / M: 22% of PODs may never automate. Mitigation: PODs sequenced last, driver photo-capture guidance at source, a permanent human lane sized for them. Owner: ops manager.
- TMS API fragility — M / H. Mitigation: sandbox revival in week two, idempotency keys, backpressure queue, shadow-file fallback; a document may be delayed, never lost. Owner: engineering.
- Supplier layout drift — H / L each, chronic in aggregate. Mitigation: per-supplier accuracy monitoring with drift alerts when an exception rate jumps; folklore rules versioned. Owner: engineering.
- The two senior clerks leave — M / H: ground truth and tribal knowledge walk out together. Mitigation: retention agreements before the project is announced, knowledge-capture sprints in month one, promotion into QA/threshold ownership. Owner: COO.
- Peak-season disruption — M / H. Mitigation: October-December change freeze, parallel-run insurance, a tested one-switch fallback to full manual. Owner: ops manager.
- Morale collapse and quiet sabotage — H / M: 18 people heard 'released by Christmas'. Mitigation: honest comms with the real 12-month plan, clerks co-design the exception UI, redeployment paths published early. Owner: COO.
- OCR vendor lock-in — L / M. Mitigation: abstraction layer over the OCR step; benchmark two options in the POC alongside the buy-versus-build test. Owner: engineering.

tasks.name: Cost estimate
tasks.prompt: Build the cost model with full arithmetic: per-document marginal cost, monthly run rate, build cost, the labour baseline, savings at your STP target with best/expected/worst, the error-cost line, payback period, and the two sensitivities that dominate.
tasks.expert:
Per-document marginal: OCR £0.001-0.01 (photos only) + extraction ~3k input / 400 output tokens ~ £0.008-0.02 + amortised infra ~ £0.005 -> £0.01-0.03 per document. At 40,000/month: £400-1,200 model and OCR; infra (workers, Postgres, Redis, object storage, monitoring) £400-700/month; ~0.2 FTE ongoing integration maintenance. Call the run rate £15-25k/year.

Build: 2 engineers x 12-14 weeks ~ £70-95k including the exception UI — do not economise there, it is where the residual 25% of documents get handled fast — plus ~£8k of clerk time for gold-set labelling.

Baseline: £580k/year labour = £1.21 per document. At 70% STP, ~10-11 FTEs of keying work is removed ~ £330-360k/year gross; net of run costs and a retained 6-8 person exception and QA team, expected ~ £280-330k/year. Error line on top: 4% error rate x ~19,200 error-prone documents x £45 average resolution ~ £86k/year today; validation rules cut it by half or better ~ £45k/year saved, plus fewer port holds.

Best case (80% STP, invoices and customs smooth): ~£420k/year. Worst (55% STP, PODs never automate): ~£190k/year — still comfortably positive, which is why this is a go at any realistic accuracy. Payback on ~£100k all-in build: three to five months at steady state.

Sensitivities: STP rate (each 10 points ~ £50k/year) and exception handle time — if the UI is clumsy and a correction takes as long as keying from scratch, savings halve; measure seconds-per-exception in the POC, not after launch.

tasks.name: POC plan
tasks.prompt: Write the POC plan: the slice and why it is that slice, gold-set construction by the senior clerks, the shadow-table design (no live posting), numeric success gates including STP precision, kill criteria, duration, and the buy-versus-build test folded in.
tasks.expert:
Slice: born-digital invoices from the top-20 suppliers — roughly 30% of all volume, the cleanest inputs, and the highest financial stakes, so the validation story is proven where it matters most. Duration: three weeks build plus one measured week.

Gold set first: 1,000 invoices double-keyed fresh by the two senior clerks, disagreements adjudicated — which doubles as writing down their supplier folklore for the first time. This is the project's measuring stick; nothing honest happens without it.

Build: intake from a copy of the mailbox, classify, extract to the eight-field schema, validate, write to a shadow table — never the live TMS — and diff daily against what the human team actually posted. The same week, run the vendor's tool on the same 1,000 documents: the buy-versus-build decision for the extraction layer gets made on reproduced numbers, not the demo.

Success gates agreed with the COO and ops manager before build: field-level accuracy 98%+ on header fields; 99.5%+ on amounts specifically; STP-eligible (all validations green, confidence above threshold) on 60%+ of POC documents with STP precision 99%+ — when the system calls a document green, it is right 99 times in 100; median exception-correction time under 90 seconds in hallway tests with real clerks.

Kill criteria: header accuracy below 90% on born-digital invoices after two iterations — the approach is wrong, stop; TMS sandbox unusable with no workaround — integration risk cannot be priced; clerk labelling unavailable — no ground truth means no honest metrics, and a dishonest POC is worse than none. Deliverable: per-field, per-supplier accuracy table plus the scale/stop memo and the buy-versus-build recommendation.

tasks.name: Evaluation & rollout
tasks.prompt: Design evaluation and rollout: the metrics that matter (including STP precision and per-supplier tracking), the correction-capture flywheel, the parallel-run and staged auto-posting plan, the peak-season freeze, the people transition, and the monthly business review.
tasks.expert:
Metrics: field-level precision and recall per document type AND per supplier — aggregate accuracy hides the one layout that broke last Tuesday. Amount fields tracked separately with a zero-silent-error target: an amount error that slips past validation pages someone, every time. STP precision (the green-but-wrong rate) guards the business; STP rate measures the benefit; they are reported as a pair, never alone. Exception-queue depth and seconds-per-correction complete the picture.

The flywheel: every correction in the exception UI is captured as a labelled pair, and a weekly re-scored eval set measures the system against fresh reality rather than the launch-day gold set. Supplier drift shows up as a rising exception rate and triggers a targeted fix, not a firefight.

Rollout: four-week parallel run — the system shadows, humans still key, daily diffs reviewed with the clerks -> auto-posting for top-20 suppliers with 4-eyes above £5k -> expand supplier-by-supplier as each clears 98% on 200+ documents -> customs forms next -> PODs last, preceded by a driver photo-quality push measured before and after. October-December change freeze; the fallback switch to full manual is tested like a fire drill, in advance, twice.

People transition runs alongside the technology: 18 -> 6-8 over twelve months via attrition and redeployment into exceptions and QA; the senior clerks own thresholds and a weekly 200-document random audit against source images.

Monthly business review: STP rate and precision, £ per document, disputes traced to extraction, exception SLA — the board gets the real number and its trend, not the vendor's brochure figure, and the Christmas conversation becomes a September one about evidence.

debrief: Strong answers segment by document type and difficulty — born-digital invoices, customs, then PODs — instead of treating '40,000 documents' as one problem, and they price the asymmetry: a wrong auto-posted amount costs more than a slow document, so STP precision outranks STP rate everywhere. They design the exception lane as a product rather than an apology, and treat the two senior clerks as the most valuable asset in the building: ground truth, folklore, and the future QA team. They reset '100% by Christmas' to 70-80% with a permanent human lane and let the arithmetic — worst case still ~£190k a year net — do the persuading. Weak answers repeat the vendor's 99.9%, auto-post from day one, skip the TMS integration and the people plan, and report aggregate accuracy where supplier-level drift hides. The blockchain deflection is worth one sentence; a paragraph on it is itself a fail.
